title: Baked fish with lemon and herbs
skill: Baking fish gently, checking pin bones

notes.text: Use two sheet pans, on racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven, and swap them halfway through.

move.title: Gentle heat, and two things done at once
move.body: Fish is tender and cooks fast, so gentle, even oven heat suits it. Today you'll feel for pin bones and pull them out, bake fillets with lemon, garlic, and dill to 145°F, and make Unit 5's rice pilaf alongside, timed so the fish comes out of the oven just as the rice is ready.

callback.body: If you made pineapple teriyaki salmon, you seared it in a hot pan and checked it at 145°F. Baking is gentler: the oven heats the fish from every side at once, so there's no flipping and less chance of drying it out.

why.title: Feel for pin bones
why.body: Fillets can hide a row of thin, soft bones running down the middle of the thick end. Run your fingertips along the fillet against the grain and you'll feel their tips. Pulled out now, nobody finds one at dinner.

why.title: Pat it dry
why.body: A wet fillet steams in its own water and turns pale. Patted dry, its outside sets nicely, and the oil and seasoning stick to it.

why.title: Thickness sets the time
why.body: Fish cooks from the outside in, and thin fish cooks fast. Allow about 10 minutes for every inch of thickness at the thickest part, and start checking early.

why.title: Work backward from the finish
why.body: The rice needs 25 minutes from the moment the lid goes on, and the fish needs about 15. Start the rice first, and put the fish in the oven 10 minutes later. Both are ready at the same time.

why.title: 145°F, and it flakes
why.body: Cooked fish turns from see-through to solid, and the flesh separates into flakes when you press it with a fork. The thermometer in the thickest part should read 145°F. Past that, fish dries out fast.

wrong.sign: The fish is still see-through in the middle
wrong.fix: Put it back in for 2 or 3 minutes and check again. Thick pieces take longer than thin ones.
It cooked past 145°F. Next time, start checking 3 minutes early, and pull thin pieces first.
Pin bones hide in the thick end. Next time, run your fingers down the fillet twice before it goes in.

wrong.sign: The fish was done long before the rice
wrong.fix: Keep it warm with foil over the pan. Next time, put the fish in when the rice timer shows 15 minutes left.

quiz.q: What temperature does fish need to reach?
quiz.explain: And it flakes when you press it with a fork.

quiz.q: Where do pin bones usually hide?
choices: In a row down the thick end of the fillet
In the thin tail end only
quiz.explain: Run your fingertips along it to feel them.

quiz.q: The rice needs 25 minutes and the fish 15. When does the fish go in?
choices: At the same time as the rice
quiz.explain: Work backward from when you want to eat.

substitutions.note: Cod is often cheaper. Thinner pieces may be done in 10 minutes.
Tilapia is thin and cheap. Start checking at 8 minutes.

steps.text: Turn the oven on to 400°F, with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan with parchment.

Put the rice in the medium bowl and cover it with cold water. Swish it with your hand, then carefully pour off the cloudy water, holding the rice back with your hand. Do this 4 or 5 times, and pour off as much water as you can.
Heat the broth in the liquid measuring cup in the microwave until it's steaming.
steps.tip: Use oven mitts to lift it out.

steps.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the rice and stir until the edges of the grains turn see-through and it smells nutty. Stand back and pour in the hot broth, add the rice's salt, and stir once.
steps.look: Glossy grains with clear edges before the broth goes in.

steps.text: Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to your lowest setting and put the lid on. Start a 25-minute timer: 15 minutes cooking, then 10 resting with the burner off. Don't lift the lid.
steps.tip: Turn the burner off when 10 minutes are left on the timer, and leave the lid on.

steps.text: While the rice cooks, grate the yellow peel of the lemon on the small holes of the grater into the small bowl. Then cut the lemon in half: slice one half into thin rounds and cut the other into wedges.
Stir the oil, garlic, dill, the fish's salt, and the pepper into the lemon zest.

Lay the fish on the lined pan and pat every side dry with paper towels. Run your fingertips along each piece, against the grain, to feel for thin bones. Pull out any you find with the tweezers, tugging toward the thick end.
steps.tip: Cod and tilapia rarely have them, but check anyway.

steps.text: Throw the paper towels and the fish's package away. Wash your hands with soap, and wash the tweezers.
Spread the lemon mixture over the tops of the fish with a spoon, and lay a lemon round on each piece. Leave space between the pieces.
When the rice timer shows 15 minutes left, slide the pan into the oven.
steps.tip: Use oven mitts, and slide the pan in away from you.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull the pan out. Slide the thermometer into the side of the thickest piece. It needs to read at least 145°F, and the fish should flake when you press it with a fork. If not, bake 2 more minutes and check again.
Fluff the rice with the fork. Lift each piece of fish onto a plate with the spatula, add rice beside it, and serve with the lemon wedges.
steps.look: The fish is solid and pale pink or white all the way through, and the rice is fluffy.
